commits.message: clarify dev + release/ship flow across README, CONTRIBUTING, dev doc
commits.body:
The release docs predated the release-gated deploy pipeline and never
explained what actually ships a build. Make the flow explicit and
consistent:

- README: "Releasing & shipping" — the two-step flow (pnpm release →
  git push --follow-tags), what the tag push triggers (GHCR images +
  Coolify), and that plain main pushes only run CI.
- releases-and-versioning.md: add a "Shipping (build & deploy)" section
  (release-gated on v* tags, image tags, manual-dispatch escape hatch);
  drop the stale "deploy as its own step" wording.
- CONTRIBUTING: note versions/changelog are release-generated (don't bump
  in PRs) + a maintainers-only Releasing pointer.

commits.message: create annotated tag so --follow-tags pushes it
commits.body:
`pnpm release` printed `git push origin main --follow-tags`, but the tag
was lightweight and --follow-tags only pushes annotated tags — so the
tag was silently left behind (e.g. v0.1.1 stranded locally). Tag with
-a so the recommended push carries commit + tag together.

  focus-guard spans that grew/shifted the brand icon.

singletons and installs a host via engenty.server.registerContextGraphHost();
core holds only the plugin-sdk contract and delegates lazily. This makes the
core host plugins-free and removes the boot-time dist build it required.

commits.message:
fix(env-setup): prefer legacy JWT keys for local Supabase (#2)

* fix(env-setup): prefer legacy JWT keys when harvesting local Supabase status

The wizard resolved Supabase keys new-format-first (SECRET_KEY/
PUBLISHABLE_KEY), writing sb_secret_/sb_publishable_ values to .env.local.
The local Supabase CLI stack's PostgREST only validates HS256 JWTs against
JWT_SECRET and rejects the single-part sb_* keys (PGRST301) unless
asymmetric signing keys are configured — so dev:env:init produced a stack
that 500s on every request to a custom schema.

resolveSupabaseValue now takes a preferJwt option; the wizard sets it when
harvesting from 'supabase status' (always the local stack) so the legacy
3-part JWT keys win. Production/example preference for the new keys is
unchanged.

* docs(dev): add setup-process guide and expand plugin lifecycle docs

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

---------

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.message:
fix(catalog-search): skip embedding when no gateway credentials

The catalog search embedding path issued a live AI Gateway call even with no
credentials, then caught the auth failure and fell back to lexical. On CI
(no API key / OIDC token) and slow shared runners that doomed round-trip could
exceed the 10s test timeout, flaking apps/ai and api tests that boot the app.

Short-circuit to lexical ranking when neither AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY nor
VERCEL_OIDC_TOKEN is set — behavior-equivalent (it fell back anyway) but fast
and deterministic, and quicker in any keyless environment. api-catalog tests
stub a key since they exercise the (mocked) embedding path.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

credentials, then caught the auth failure and fell back to lexical. On CI
(no API key / OIDC token) and slow shared runners that doomed round-trip could
exceed the 10s test timeout, flaking apps/ai and api tests that boot the app.

Short-circuit to lexical ranking when neither AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY nor
VERCEL_OIDC_TOKEN is set — behavior-equivalent (it fell back anyway) but fast
and deterministic, and quicker in any keyless environment. api-catalog tests
stub a key since they exercise the (mocked) embedding path.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.message:
fix(ci): run project setup script, not pnpm's builtin 'setup'

`pnpm setup` invokes pnpm's reserved built-in (configures PNPM_HOME), so the
project's "setup" script ('pnpm engenty setup') never ran in CI. That meant
supabase/migrations was never aggregated, so migration-reading tests
(supabase-sync-lib, live-cache) failed with ENOENT and createApp-based AI tests
hung. Use 'pnpm run setup' to invoke the package script.

This is why main's CI was red since the workflow landed.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.message:
feat(cli): plugins install — surface db migrate next-step + opt-in --db-migrate

`plugins install` aggregates module migrations but never applies them, which
surprised users (install OK, UI then throws "Invalid schema"). After installing
in-repo workspace modules it now prints the next step ("run pnpm db:migrate"),
and a new opt-in `--db-migrate` flag applies them locally — gated on a reachable
local DB so install stays DB-free for CI, fresh checkouts, and remote databases.

feat(ui-plugin-sdk): add tab contributions (UiTabContribution)

Generic, surface-keyed tab registry mirroring the existing dashboardWidgets/
settingsItems contribution chain. A module contributes a tab to another
surface (e.g. "projects.detail") via engenty.UI.registerTab; the tab only
exists while the contributing plugin is enabled, so hosts get install-gated
tabs with no feature flag or availability check on their side.

- UiTabContribution + UiTabRenderProps types; tabs added to UiContributions,
  UiEventMap ("ui.tabs"), and EngentyUiApi.registerTab
- registerTab impl + resolve emit in engenty-ui-api; normalizeTabs dedupes per
  (surface, id) and warns on collisions; stale-owner cleanup + reload pruning
- resolver/queries/context empties carry tabs; tests cover collection,
  disabled-plugin gating, and per-surface dedupe

commits.message:
fix(copilot): keep floating avatar FAB on-screen

The Copilot floating avatar (CopilotFabTrigger) applied its persisted
`fabPosition` verbatim. A position saved on a larger window rendered the
FAB off the viewport edge on a smaller one, so the avatar silently
disappeared with no recovery. The existing viewport-clamp only covered
the open floating drawer, never the collapsed FAB.

Clamp the persisted position to the current viewport when resolving the
FAB anchor (re-applied on resize) and in resolveTriggerAnchor so drag
origin and speed-dial centering match the rendered position. Also reset
collapseToCircle when the drawer is open so the two states can't conflict.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.message:
fix(copilot): make drawer robust before layout hydration and sidebar mount

Harden copilot surface mounting against two races:

- Gate CopilotDrawerLayer until the persisted `copilot.layout` snapshot is
  applied (`copilotLayoutApplied`) so the drawer/FAB don't render with a
  stale default position before hydration.
- Track inline-sidebar mount state (`copilotSidebarReady` +
  notifySidebarMounted/Unmounted) to re-render when the portal target
  attaches, and fall back to the drawer SidePanel when the sidebar
  container isn't available while open (extracted `renderDrawerFallback`).
- Reconcile the persisted layout snapshot via reconcileCopilotLayoutSnapshot
  before applying it.

commits.message:
Add --db-restart to plugins install for schema exposure

Applying a module's migrations creates its tables, but the running API
only serves schemas listed in config.toml db-schemas, read at boot — so a
newly installed module's schema stays unreachable until the stack restarts.

Add an opt-in --db-restart flag (pair with --db-migrate) and an engenty
db restart subcommand that stop/starts the local stack so PostgREST
reloads the exposed schemas. Gated on a reachable local database, matching
the existing --db-migrate opt-in.

  alive for frontend-tool resume.

CLI child-run delegation with sandbox sync-out, decision interrupt and
resume.

Four focused docs/wip analyses against @mastra/core 1.48:

  generation, resource-scope working memory (adapter already carries the
  field), tool-call filter/token limiter processors, and Observational
  Memory via pg-delegated OM record storage; semantic recall skipped in
  favor of OM retrieval.
- approvals: converge the four HITL mechanisms onto native
  suspend/resume - the 1.48 input-aware requireApproval predicate can
  gate per operation, so the abort-and-rerun decision-artifact flow can
  be deleted; contracts/grants remain the policy source; suspended runs
  survive restarts via the pg workflows domain.
- file-based agents: keep the defineModuleAi convention (superset);
  adopt createSkill; note the pure assembleAgentFromFsEntry seam.
- Code Mode: generate typed per-operation tools from the contract
  catalog, read-only allow-list first on the task specialist, writes
  stay outside Code Mode.

respects the project's external/read-only view like legacy did.

consistent with how every other tab in that dialog behaves.

commits.message:
Extract Select's glass background into a shared .ui-canvas-glass class

The glass variant's background+blur was hardcoded inline in select.tsx's
cva config, so DropdownMenu/Popover/HoverCard couldn't reuse it without
copy-pasting the Tailwind string. Add .ui-canvas-glass to
ui-canvas-chrome.css as a sibling of the existing .ui-canvas-floating,
same pattern, so any floating surface can opt in later.

Scoped to background + backdrop-filter only (no box-shadow): a plain CSS
box-shadow in that class does NOT compose with Tailwind's ring-*/shadow-*
utilities — both set the box-shadow property outright, so whichever
cascades last wins and the other is silently dropped. Discovered this
after the glass variant's ring-1 was clobbering .ui-canvas-glass's own
box-shadow entirely (verified via computed styles: only the ring layer
survived, the elevation shadow vanished). Shadow/ring/radius stay as
Tailwind utilities per consumer so they keep composing correctly.

commits.message:
Fix copilot voice call races and duplicate FAB surface

Two issues in the realtime voice session:
- OpenAI refuses response.create while a response is already in flight
  (conversation_already_has_active_response) — queue the request instead
  of sending it immediately after a tool-call result, flush on the next
  response.done.
- That error (and response_cancel_not_active) left the data channel and
  audio fully usable, but the hook was tearing down the whole session on
  any 'error' status — now only genuinely fatal errors end the call.

Also: the voice FAB and a floating call-strip composer override could
both be visible at once (e.g. shell reports closed while a call strip is
mounted) — track call-strip presence via CopilotVoiceProvider and hide
the FAB while one is mounted, so there's a single voice surface.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.message:
Surface OpenAI error details when the realtime WebRTC call fails

The realtime calls POST discarded the response body on failure, so a 429
read the same for rate limits and exhausted quota. Parse the OpenAI

Add the deploy/ bundle for VPS/Coolify deployment

Ports the full deployment bundle the public docs already reference
(docs/content/setup/coolify.md, deploy/.env.example header): a Compose
stack served through a single engenty-edge gateway (port 8787) plus the
engenty-ai runtime, with optional docs/studio/sandbox images.

  defaults off (ENGENTY_GATEWAY_MANAGE_ENABLED=false) in both compose and

  boot; TURBO_BUILD_CONCURRENCY caps parallelism on small builders.

  /manage references) from the Coolify guide.

the intended 404 on /manage; engenty-ai reports healthy on /ai/health;
deploy/.env.example matches the env manifest (env:example:check passes).

commits.message:
Move API-catalog semantic search from apps/core to apps/ai

Core keeps catalog building and its gateway method but ranks lexically
only (drops the ai package + embedding calls; no AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY
needed in core). apps/ai now applies the full ranking on the agent path:
shared lexical BM25 (extracted to @engenty/search-index) plus semantic
embedding reranking with lexical fallback, over the tenant-gated
contracts fetched from core. Contract sources are pluggable
(CatalogContractSource) so external API catalogs can merge into the same
ranked catalog later; a 60s per-bearer cache fronts the core fetch.

commits.message:
fix(copilot): dock floating launcher & avatar to bottom-right on mode switch

The floating compact launcher was positioned from floatingPosition, whose
default was sized to the modal (FLOATING_DEFAULT_HEIGHT=148) while the launcher
renders at ~56px — so switching to floating dropped it mid-screen, and nothing
re-cornered either surface on mode changes.

- Size the launcher's bottom-right home to its own footprint via
  resolveLauncherCornerPosition (used for the initial position too).
- Re-dock both surfaces to the corner when switching to floating/mini-floating
  from the position menu (launcher via floatingPosition, avatar via clearing
  fabPosition/anchor).
- Add a floatingDockedToCorner flag + layout effect that keeps the resting
  launcher pinned as its measured height settles; cleared once the user drags.
- reanchorFloatingPositionToViewport keeps a corner-docked panel tracking its
  edges on window resize instead of only clamping.

Verified in-app: switch->floating, switch->avatar, and reload all land
bottom-right; window resize tracks the corner.

commits.message:
Replace the routine scheduler with Triggers backed by Mastra heartbeats

A Trigger is the single model for 'a reason work starts' (schedule |
event | manual) and always references a task template — firing a
trigger materializes a Task into the durable task pipeline. There are
no prompt-only routines.

- tasks module: module_tasks.triggers + task_templates (schema, DAL,
  gateway operations incl. triggers_fire as the one execution path
  shared by scheduled, manual, and future event fires).
- apps/ai src/scheduler/: Mastra heartbeats as the pure cron substrate.
  The prepare hook enforces quiet hours, fires the trigger via the
  service principal, and returns null so no agent ever runs; a no-op
  engenty.scheduler agent anchors the heartbeats (worker requirement).
  Reconcile syncs module ROUTINE.md declarations -> trigger rows ->
  heartbeats at boot (deferred: the module capability loader blocks
  during createApp) and on demand via POST /ai/v1/triggers/reconcile.
- /ai/v1/triggers routes replace /ai/v1/routines; system jobs
  (cleanup-interrupts) ride their own heartbeats; the pg_cron tick,
  due.ts cron parsing, ai.routine_state and ai.custom_routine are
  dropped (core migration). cron-parser dependency removed — Engenty
  parses no cron anymore.
- routines UI now speaks the trigger API: single schedule per routine,
  task-template payloads (name doubles as task title, instructions as
  task description).
- fix: the Session workspace fallback from the 1.48 migration threw at
  runtime ('Workspace requires at least a filesystem, sandbox, or
  skills') on runs without a workspace, e.g. headless task jobs — now a
  shared scratch-dir LocalFilesystem workspace that feeds no tools.

Validated live: trigger created via UI and API -> heartbeat row ->
minute-cron fire -> task materialized with correct template fields ->
dispatch consumer -> task-job workflow -> specialist run -> in_review;
enable/disable pause-resume, delete removes the heartbeat, boot
reconcile recreates system-job heartbeats.

commits.message:
Converge tool approvals onto native Mastra suspend/resume

Replace the abort-and-rerun decision-artifact approval flow with native
tool-level suspend/resume: engenty_tool_execute declares suspend/resume
schemas and suspends the run when a contract requires approval. The
Approve/Deny decision resumes the SAME parked run in place via
respondToToolSuspension — no re-run, no lost turn.

- approvalPolicy on the engenty-tools run context (suspend | deny |
  artifact; default deny, fail-safe): interactive chat suspends,
  delegated leaf runs deny (would deadlock the parent), voice keeps its
  artifact + /v1/realtime/tools/approve flow.
- Tool-approval interrupts persist as decision-kind open interrupts
  carrying the suspended run_id; the runs route routes them to the
  parked-session resume (not the artifact re-run branch), folds the
  Approve once/always grant into session metadata, and audits the
  decision. The write-back on interrupt-clear carries the just-persisted
  grant so it survives the resume.
- resumeConversationRun drives the continuation inside the engenty-tools
  ALS context so a second gated call in the continuation suspends again
  instead of being denied, with persisted grants threaded through.
- Full-page copilot chat: fall back to the persisted open interrupt when
  the transcript has no decision artifact to render (the suspended tool
  call has no result), matching the drawer.
- Restart recovery via listSuspendedRuns is deferred; parked sessions
  keep the frontend-tool 15-min TTL (documented in docs/wip).

commits.message:
Guard engenty_tool_execute against empty tool-call input

Some models/providers drop function-call arguments entirely (observed
100% reproducible with minimax/minimax-m3: every engenty_tool_execute
call arrives with input {}). The empty input previously reached core and
surfaced as a raw zod validation error the model retried verbatim.

- Reject an empty input object before the approval gate when the
  operation contract declares required fields, with a factual message
  naming the missing fields and the likely cause (the current model's
  function calling) so the agent reports it to the user instead of
  looping on validation errors. Never asks for approval on a doomed call.
- Give the execute tool's input field a real object schema
  (z.record) instead of z.unknown(), which serialized to an empty JSON
  schema in the tool definition. (Verified this alone does not fix
  MiniMax — the arguments are dropped provider-side — but the tool
  definition is now correct for schema-strict providers.)

commits.message:
Show the voice approval dialog in threadless voice sessions

A voice session started on a fresh chat has no active thread, and the
voice provider only parked a gated backend op's approval for the
confirmation dialog when a thread existed — without one, the raw
decision artifact went back to the voice model, which then narrated an
on-screen dialog that never rendered.

The dialog now always shows. With a thread, the decision persists as a
chat grant as before ('always' survives the whole chat). Without one,
the grant cannot be persisted, so the user's dialog decision rides the
re-invoke as a one-shot approval_grant_once on the execute call — the
same authority as the persisted-grant path (an explicit user decision on
the user's own bearer token), scoped to that single call.

commits.message:
Add event triggers: module-event bus + webhook ingestion onto triggers_fire

Phase 2 of the trigger cutover — event triggers fire the same
triggers_fire task materialization as schedule and manual triggers,
through two ingestion edges:

- provider_id 'module-events': the tasks plugin subscribes to the
  in-process plugin event bus (engenty.events.modules) for every
  canonical event name an enabled trigger listens to (exact-name
  subscriptions, replayed from the database on boot, extended on
  trigger create/update), applies the shallow event_filter payload
  match, and fires per matching tenant trigger.
- provider_id 'webhook': a public tasks-module route
  POST /api/tasks/trigger-hooks/:triggerId/:secret, authenticated by a
  per-trigger secret generated at creation (timing-safe compare, one
  generic 401 for every reject reason).

Both edges attach the event payload to the materialized task's
description so the agent works on the concrete occurrence. The fire
logic is extracted from the triggers_fire gateway op into a shared
fireTrigger (scoped to the trigger row's own tenant/scope), used by all
callers including the heartbeat hook path.

Mastra SignalProviders are deliberately NOT used: compiled-dist
verification showed they are thread-scoped (every subscription is a
(resourceId, threadId), delivery is sendNotificationSignal into a
thread, the documented POST /api/signals/:providerId route does not
exist in the shipped 1.48 build, and subscriptions are in-memory). A
trigger has no thread — its effect is materializing a Task. Signals are
adopted where they fit: the notifications/inbox phase. Design revision
recorded in docs/wip/agent-ops-target-architecture.md.

UI: the routines feature gains a trigger-type selector (schedule /
module event / inbound webhook), event name + JSON payload filter
fields, event chips in the list, and the webhook URL on the detail
page.

Live-validated: contacts_create → contacts.contact.created → task
materialized with payload + auto-dispatched; webhook fire with wrong
secret 401, right secret 200 + task with body attached.

  per-trigger secret generated at creation (timing-safe compare, one
  generic 401 for every reject reason).

Both edges attach the event payload to the materialized task's
description so the agent works on the concrete occurrence. The fire
logic is extracted from the triggers_fire gateway op into a shared
fireTrigger (scoped to the trigger row's own tenant/scope), used by all
callers including the heartbeat hook path.

Mastra SignalProviders are deliberately NOT used: compiled-dist
verification showed they are thread-scoped (every subscription is a
(resourceId, threadId), delivery is sendNotificationSignal into a
thread, the documented POST /api/signals/:providerId route does not
exist in the shipped 1.48 build, and subscriptions are in-memory). A
trigger has no thread — its effect is materializing a Task. Signals are
adopted where they fit: the notifications/inbox phase. Design revision
recorded in docs/wip/agent-ops-target-architecture.md.

UI: the routines feature gains a trigger-type selector (schedule /
module event / inbound webhook), event name + JSON payload filter
fields, event chips in the list, and the webhook URL on the detail
page.

Live-validated: contacts_create → contacts.contact.created → task
materialized with payload + auto-dispatched; webhook fire with wrong
secret 401, right secret 200 + task with body attached.

commits.message:
Add notifications inbox on Mastra notifications storage

Task completions/failures and trigger errors now land in a durable team
inbox instead of only in task rows nobody watches.

Backend (apps/ai):
- src/notifications/inbox.ts — records created DIRECTLY on the Mastra
  notifications storage domain (ai.mastra_notifications), not via
  sendNotificationSignal (that is agent-to-agent delivery machinery:
  forces agentId, runs delivery policy, wakes threads). Records carry no
  deliverAt/summaryAt, so the built-in notification dispatcher never
  considers them due. Scoping rides a synthetic per-tenant inbox thread
  (inbox:{tenantId}) — the table has no tenant column and only filters
  on threadId/resourceId/agentId. The storage handle is imported lazily:
  the emitters sit inside the Mastra config's own dependency graph and
  an eager singleton import is a circular module-eval.
- Emitters: task-job finalize emits task_completed / task_failed (with
  result text payload and task metadata for deep links); the heartbeat
  onError hook emits trigger_failed, deduped per trigger while pending
  so a crashing schedule coalesces into one entry.
- /ai/v1/notifications routes: list, unseen-count, seen-all, per-id
  seen/dismiss — thin over the storage domain, tenant from the bearer.

Shell: admin-menu contributions accept a useBadgeCount hook, rendered by
an always-mounted per-item badge component on the app-bar icon rail
(first badge mechanism in the shell).

Tasks module UI: Posteingang/Inbox page (/mdl/tasks/inbox) with mark
seen/dismiss + mark-all, a sidebar item after Briefing with an unseen
count badge, an open-notifications section on the Briefing screen, and
the unseen badge on the tasks app-bar icon. Data layer (fetch + query
hooks) lives in ai-ui features/inbox, same split as routines.

Live-validated: webhook trigger -> task ENG-55 -> agent completed ->
task_completed record -> badges (app bar + sidebar), Briefing section,
inbox page; mark-all-seen persists and clears both badges.

fix(copilot): dock floating launcher & avatar to bottom-right on mode switch

The floating compact launcher was positioned from floatingPosition, whose
default was sized to the modal (FLOATING_DEFAULT_HEIGHT=148) while the launcher
renders at ~56px — so switching to floating dropped it mid-screen, and nothing
re-cornered either surface on mode changes.

  resolveLauncherCornerPosition (used for the initial position too).

  fabPosition/anchor).

  launcher pinned as its measured height settles; cleared once the user drags.

  edges on window resize instead of only clamping.

bottom-right; window resize tracks the corner.

commits.message:
Adopt Mastra memory quick wins: thread titles, working memory, history hygiene

Three memory adoptions on the chat substrate, verified against the
compiled @mastra/memory 1.21 / core 1.48 dist before wiring:

- Thread title generation: memory options.generateTitle synthesizes the
  title from the first exchange using the agent's own model (compiled
  fallback via getLLM when model is omitted); fires only while the
  thread is untitled. The two legacy title paths are DELETED so they
  cannot block the gate: the client-side first-message truncation
  (deriveInitialSessionTitleFromText / deriveInitialThreadTitleFromText,
  incl. the dead server-side maybeDeriveInitialSessionTitle orphan) —
  threads are now created untitled and lists fall back to summary/id
  until the title lands.

- Working memory (resource scope): a small bounded zod profile
  (language, role, focus, preferences, facts) injected each turn and
  maintained by the agent via the auto-registered updateWorkingMemory
  tool. The adapter's stub resource methods now persist for real by
  delegating to the pg memory domain (ai.mastra_resources), keyed
  `${tenantId}:${userId}` so profiles stay tenant-scoped while the
  Mastra resourceId remains the engenty user id. Settings view
  (Assistant memory) renders the profile read-only with a reset button,
  backed by GET/DELETE /ai/v1/memory/working.

- History hygiene on every assembled agent: ToolCallFilter strips bulky
  engenty_tool_execute transcripts from recalled history (the last two
  tool steps stay intact for the live loop) and TokenLimiterProcessor
  caps recalled history at 100k tokens.

Live-validated: German first message → synthesized German title
("Aktuelle zeitgesteuerte Routinen"); "merke dir…" turn → agent wrote
the schema profile to ai.mastra_resources; settings page renders it and
reset clears it.

commits.message:
Add Code Mode (read-only) on the copilot's Docker workspace sandbox

One `execute_typescript` tool: the model writes a single TypeScript
program that orchestrates tools as external_* functions in the run's
workspace sandbox — batching, filtering, and aggregation happen in code
instead of N chat round-trips.

- Tool set (v1): the discovery meta-tool (engenty_tools_search) plus a
  READ-ONLY execute variant (engenty_tool_execute_readonly). The
  read-only allow-list is enforced server-side in executeEngentyTool
  ({enforceReadOnly}) — non-read-only operations (risk above low, or
  approval-gated) are rejected with a clear pointer to the regular chat
  tool where the native approval gate applies. Typed per-operation
  stubs generated from contract JSON schemas are a later enhancement.

- DockerCodeModeTransport: the shipped StdioCodeModeTransport stages
  the program on the HOST and spawns node against a host path — which a
  Docker sandbox cannot see. This transport speaks the same wire
  protocol (frames on stdout, rpc-results on stdin; runner source from
  the exported buildRunner/buildProgramModule) but stages into the
  sandbox's bind-mounted working directory, lazily starts the
  container, and runs the program with bun (the unified sandbox image
  ships it). Host↔container path mapping is read from the pinned
  DockerSandbox instance fields — documented compiled-behavior
  coupling, re-verify per @mastra bump.

- Attach rule: root agents that carry the engenty catalog meta-tools
  AND run with a sandbox-carrying workspace; the code-mode usage
  contract + external_* stubs are appended to their instructions.

- The copilot workspace now enables the sandbox (session lifecycle,
  lazy container start — idle chats pay nothing). EXECUTE_COMMAND keeps
  its HITL approval gate; free-form CLI/code work stays delegated to
  the engenty.cli sub-agent.

Live-validated: one prompt → three iterating programs in the container
(a real TypeError propagated back through the RPC bridge, console.log
lines streamed as frames, then a program fetched all contacts via
external_engenty_tool_execute_readonly and aggregated in code) → one
correct result. Unit test covers the read-only guard both ways.

commits.message:
Replace the routine scheduler with Triggers backed by Mastra heartbeats

A Trigger is the single model for 'a reason work starts' (schedule |
event | manual) and always references a task template — firing a
trigger materializes a Task into the durable task pipeline. There are
no prompt-only routines.

- tasks module: module_tasks.triggers + task_templates (schema, DAL,
  gateway operations incl. triggers_fire as the one execution path
  shared by scheduled, manual, and future event fires).
- apps/ai src/scheduler/: Mastra heartbeats as the pure cron substrate.
  The prepare hook enforces quiet hours, fires the trigger via the
  service principal, and returns null so no agent ever runs; a no-op
  engenty.scheduler agent anchors the heartbeats (worker requirement).
  Reconcile syncs module ROUTINE.md declarations -> trigger rows ->
  heartbeats at boot (deferred: the module capability loader blocks
  during createApp) and on demand via POST /ai/v1/triggers/reconcile.
- /ai/v1/triggers routes replace /ai/v1/routines; system jobs
  (cleanup-interrupts) ride their own heartbeats; the pg_cron tick,
  due.ts cron parsing, ai.routine_state and ai.custom_routine are
  dropped (core migration). cron-parser dependency removed — Engenty
  parses no cron anymore.
- routines UI now speaks the trigger API: single schedule per routine,
  task-template payloads (name doubles as task title, instructions as
  task description).
- fix: the Session workspace fallback from the 1.48 migration threw at
  runtime ('Workspace requires at least a filesystem, sandbox, or
  skills') on runs without a workspace, e.g. headless task jobs — now a
  shared scratch-dir LocalFilesystem workspace that feeds no tools.

Validated live: trigger created via UI and API -> heartbeat row ->
minute-cron fire -> task materialized with correct template fields ->
dispatch consumer -> task-job workflow -> specialist run -> in_review;
enable/disable pause-resume, delete removes the heartbeat, boot
reconcile recreates system-job heartbeats.

commits.message:
Converge tool approvals onto native Mastra suspend/resume

Replace the abort-and-rerun decision-artifact approval flow with native
tool-level suspend/resume: engenty_tool_execute declares suspend/resume
schemas and suspends the run when a contract requires approval. The
Approve/Deny decision resumes the SAME parked run in place via
respondToToolSuspension — no re-run, no lost turn.

- approvalPolicy on the engenty-tools run context (suspend | deny |
  artifact; default deny, fail-safe): interactive chat suspends,
  delegated leaf runs deny (would deadlock the parent), voice keeps its
  artifact + /v1/realtime/tools/approve flow.
- Tool-approval interrupts persist as decision-kind open interrupts
  carrying the suspended run_id; the runs route routes them to the
  parked-session resume (not the artifact re-run branch), folds the
  Approve once/always grant into session metadata, and audits the
  decision. The write-back on interrupt-clear carries the just-persisted
  grant so it survives the resume.
- resumeConversationRun drives the continuation inside the engenty-tools
  ALS context so a second gated call in the continuation suspends again
  instead of being denied, with persisted grants threaded through.
- Full-page copilot chat: fall back to the persisted open interrupt when
  the transcript has no decision artifact to render (the suspended tool
  call has no result), matching the drawer.
- Restart recovery via listSuspendedRuns is deferred; parked sessions
  keep the frontend-tool 15-min TTL (documented in docs/wip).

commits.message:
Guard engenty_tool_execute against empty tool-call input

Some models/providers drop function-call arguments entirely (observed
100% reproducible with minimax/minimax-m3: every engenty_tool_execute
call arrives with input {}). The empty input previously reached core and
surfaced as a raw zod validation error the model retried verbatim.

- Reject an empty input object before the approval gate when the
  operation contract declares required fields, with a factual message
  naming the missing fields and the likely cause (the current model's
  function calling) so the agent reports it to the user instead of
  looping on validation errors. Never asks for approval on a doomed call.
- Give the execute tool's input field a real object schema
  (z.record) instead of z.unknown(), which serialized to an empty JSON
  schema in the tool definition. (Verified this alone does not fix
  MiniMax — the arguments are dropped provider-side — but the tool
  definition is now correct for schema-strict providers.)

commits.message:
Show the voice approval dialog in threadless voice sessions

A voice session started on a fresh chat has no active thread, and the
voice provider only parked a gated backend op's approval for the
confirmation dialog when a thread existed — without one, the raw
decision artifact went back to the voice model, which then narrated an
on-screen dialog that never rendered.

The dialog now always shows. With a thread, the decision persists as a
chat grant as before ('always' survives the whole chat). Without one,
the grant cannot be persisted, so the user's dialog decision rides the
re-invoke as a one-shot approval_grant_once on the execute call — the
same authority as the persisted-grant path (an explicit user decision on
the user's own bearer token), scoped to that single call.

  in-process plugin event bus (engenty.events.modules) for every
  canonical event name an enabled trigger listens to (exact-name
  subscriptions, replayed from the database on boot, extended on
  trigger create/update), applies the shallow event_filter payload
  match, and fires per matching tenant trigger.
- provider_id 'webhook': a public tasks-module route
  POST /api/tasks/trigger-hooks/:triggerId/:secret, authenticated by a
  per-trigger secret generated at creation (timing-safe compare, one
  generic 401 for every reject reason).

Both edges attach the event payload to the materialized task's
description so the agent works on the concrete occurrence. The fire
logic is extracted from the triggers_fire gateway op into a shared
fireTrigger (scoped to the trigger row's own tenant/scope), used by all
callers including the heartbeat hook path.

Mastra SignalProviders are deliberately NOT used: compiled-dist
verification showed they are thread-scoped (every subscription is a
(resourceId, threadId), delivery is sendNotificationSignal into a
thread, the documented POST /api/signals/:providerId route does not
exist in the shipped 1.48 build, and subscriptions are in-memory). A
trigger has no thread — its effect is materializing a Task. Signals are
adopted where they fit: the notifications/inbox phase. Design revision
recorded in docs/wip/agent-ops-target-architecture.md.

UI: the routines feature gains a trigger-type selector (schedule /
module event / inbound webhook), event name + JSON payload filter
fields, event chips in the list, and the webhook URL on the detail
page.

Live-validated: contacts_create → contacts.contact.created → task
materialized with payload + auto-dispatched; webhook fire with wrong
secret 401, right secret 200 + task with body attached.

commits.message:
Add notifications inbox on Mastra notifications storage

Task completions/failures and trigger errors now land in a durable team
inbox instead of only in task rows nobody watches.

Backend (apps/ai):
- src/notifications/inbox.ts — records created DIRECTLY on the Mastra
  notifications storage domain (ai.mastra_notifications), not via
  sendNotificationSignal (that is agent-to-agent delivery machinery:
  forces agentId, runs delivery policy, wakes threads). Records carry no
  deliverAt/summaryAt, so the built-in notification dispatcher never
  considers them due. Scoping rides a synthetic per-tenant inbox thread
  (inbox:{tenantId}) — the table has no tenant column and only filters
  on threadId/resourceId/agentId. The storage handle is imported lazily:
  the emitters sit inside the Mastra config's own dependency graph and
  an eager singleton import is a circular module-eval.
- Emitters: task-job finalize emits task_completed / task_failed (with
  result text payload and task metadata for deep links); the heartbeat
  onError hook emits trigger_failed, deduped per trigger while pending
  so a crashing schedule coalesces into one entry.
- /ai/v1/notifications routes: list, unseen-count, seen-all, per-id
  seen/dismiss — thin over the storage domain, tenant from the bearer.

Shell: admin-menu contributions accept a useBadgeCount hook, rendered by
an always-mounted per-item badge component on the app-bar icon rail
(first badge mechanism in the shell).

Tasks module UI: Posteingang/Inbox page (/mdl/tasks/inbox) with mark
seen/dismiss + mark-all, a sidebar item after Briefing with an unseen
count badge, an open-notifications section on the Briefing screen, and
the unseen badge on the tasks app-bar icon. Data layer (fetch + query
hooks) lives in ai-ui features/inbox, same split as routines.

Live-validated: webhook trigger -> task ENG-55 -> agent completed ->
task_completed record -> badges (app bar + sidebar), Briefing section,
inbox page; mark-all-seen persists and clears both badges.

commits.message:
Adopt Mastra memory quick wins: thread titles, working memory, history hygiene

Three memory adoptions on the chat substrate, verified against the
compiled @mastra/memory 1.21 / core 1.48 dist before wiring:

- Thread title generation: memory options.generateTitle synthesizes the
  title from the first exchange using the agent's own model (compiled
  fallback via getLLM when model is omitted); fires only while the
  thread is untitled. The two legacy title paths are DELETED so they
  cannot block the gate: the client-side first-message truncation
  (deriveInitialSessionTitleFromText / deriveInitialThreadTitleFromText,
  incl. the dead server-side maybeDeriveInitialSessionTitle orphan) —
  threads are now created untitled and lists fall back to summary/id
  until the title lands.

- Working memory (resource scope): a small bounded zod profile
  (language, role, focus, preferences, facts) injected each turn and
  maintained by the agent via the auto-registered updateWorkingMemory
  tool. The adapter's stub resource methods now persist for real by
  delegating to the pg memory domain (ai.mastra_resources), keyed
  `${tenantId}:${userId}` so profiles stay tenant-scoped while the
  Mastra resourceId remains the engenty user id. Settings view
  (Assistant memory) renders the profile read-only with a reset button,
  backed by GET/DELETE /ai/v1/memory/working.

- History hygiene on every assembled agent: ToolCallFilter strips bulky
  engenty_tool_execute transcripts from recalled history (the last two
  tool steps stay intact for the live loop) and TokenLimiterProcessor
  caps recalled history at 100k tokens.

Live-validated: German first message → synthesized German title
("Aktuelle zeitgesteuerte Routinen"); "merke dir…" turn → agent wrote
the schema profile to ai.mastra_resources; settings page renders it and
reset clears it.

commits.message:
Add Code Mode (read-only) on the copilot's Docker workspace sandbox

One `execute_typescript` tool: the model writes a single TypeScript
program that orchestrates tools as external_* functions in the run's
workspace sandbox — batching, filtering, and aggregation happen in code
instead of N chat round-trips.

- Tool set (v1): the discovery meta-tool (engenty_tools_search) plus a
  READ-ONLY execute variant (engenty_tool_execute_readonly). The
  read-only allow-list is enforced server-side in executeEngentyTool
  ({enforceReadOnly}) — non-read-only operations (risk above low, or
  approval-gated) are rejected with a clear pointer to the regular chat
  tool where the native approval gate applies. Typed per-operation
  stubs generated from contract JSON schemas are a later enhancement.

- DockerCodeModeTransport: the shipped StdioCodeModeTransport stages
  the program on the HOST and spawns node against a host path — which a
  Docker sandbox cannot see. This transport speaks the same wire
  protocol (frames on stdout, rpc-results on stdin; runner source from
  the exported buildRunner/buildProgramModule) but stages into the
  sandbox's bind-mounted working directory, lazily starts the
  container, and runs the program with bun (the unified sandbox image
  ships it). Host↔container path mapping is read from the pinned
  DockerSandbox instance fields — documented compiled-behavior
  coupling, re-verify per @mastra bump.

- Attach rule: root agents that carry the engenty catalog meta-tools
  AND run with a sandbox-carrying workspace; the code-mode usage
  contract + external_* stubs are appended to their instructions.

- The copilot workspace now enables the sandbox (session lifecycle,
  lazy container start — idle chats pay nothing). EXECUTE_COMMAND keeps
  its HITL approval gate; free-form CLI/code work stays delegated to
  the engenty.cli sub-agent.

Live-validated: one prompt → three iterating programs in the container
(a real TypeError propagated back through the RPC bridge, console.log
lines streamed as frames, then a program fetched all contacts via
external_engenty_tool_execute_readonly and aggregated in code) → one
correct result. Unit test covers the read-only guard both ways.

commits.message:
Retry scheduler service-scope resolution to survive the dev boot race

startScheduler() resolved the service principal's scope exactly once at
boot. When the AI app boots ahead of core in the turbo dev stack, the
core HTTP call fails (network_error, status 0), the scope resolves to
null, and the scheduler stays disabled for the whole process with only a
warning.

resolveSchedulerServiceScope() now distinguishes a missing
ENGENTY_AI_SERVICE_JWT (permanent — warn once, stay off) from a failed
resolution (core unreachable / JWT rejected — transient), and
startScheduler() retries the transient case on a bounded backoff
mirroring the existing reconcile deferral before giving up. The
resolution result is returned as a discriminated union so the two cases
log distinctly.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.message:
Add the external connections framework: central OAuth, per-action policies, connectors

One mechanism for external service connections, extensible via connector
modules, with a three-axis permission model enforced at the existing
operation gate (design: docs/wip/connections-framework.md).

- @engenty/connections-sdk: ConnectorDefinition/actions (read|write|
  destructive groups drive the static contract), globalThis-backed
  connector registry (per-plugin jiti module caches would otherwise
  split a module-level singleton), AES-256-GCM token crypto
  (CONNECTIONS_TOKEN_ENC_KEY), generic OAuth2 client, module_connections
  repo (withFreshAccessToken is the only token read path), allow/ask/
  deny policy resolution (action override > group override > default,
  with sharing and autonomous-mode clamps), and the runtime that
  projects connector actions into module operations.
- modules/connections: schema (connections, connection_action_policies,
  pending_oauth_flows, approval_requests; token columns excluded from
  the authenticated column grant), nonce-state OAuth connect/callback
  routes, management operations (catalog, settings, set_policy,
  disconnect, approvals list/decide, granted_operations), and the async
  profile policy: deny clamps are authoritative for every principal;
  user asks stay with the AI pre-gate; autonomous asks 202 and record a
  durable approval request. UI: settings + admin pages with the
  per-action allow/ask/deny matrix, sharing, autonomous mode, non-owner
  cap, pending-approvals table (en+de).
- Connectors: google (gmail/drive/calendar), microsoft (outlook mail+
  calendar, onedrive via Graph), slack (user-token, scopes via
  user_scope).
- Core: profile policies may be async (evaluatePolicy awaited at its
  three call sites).
- AI plane: chat/resume runs merge durable connection grants into the
  approval grants so 'always allow' skips the Approve card; new
  approvalPolicy 'defer' for headless task jobs passes gated calls
  through to core and shapes the 202 into an approval_pending result
  plus a tenant-inbox notification. Delegated in-chat leaf runs keep
  'deny'.

Follow-up (documented): automatic task re-dispatch on approval; MCP
connector kind.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

  routes, management operations (catalog, settings, set_policy,

  profile policy: deny clamps are authoritative for every principal;
  user asks stay with the AI pre-gate; autonomous asks 202 and record a
  durable approval request. UI: settings + admin pages with the
  per-action allow/ask/deny matrix, sharing, autonomous mode, non-owner
  cap, pending-approvals table (en+de).

  calendar, onedrive via Graph), slack (user-token, scopes via
  user_scope).

  three call sites).

  approval grants so 'always allow' skips the Approve card; new

  plus a tenant-inbox notification. Delegated in-chat leaf runs keep
  'deny'.

connector kind.

The offers.manager skills were written against offers_list/get/create/
update/get_blocks/replace_blocks/… — but the module only registered HTTP
routes, which never enter the tools catalog, so agents had ZERO backend
access to offers (invoices had the full layer; offers lost it in the
migration). Register the gateway methods (invoices pattern):

- reads: offers_list, offers_get (id or offer number), offers_get_blocks,
  offers_get_next_number
- writes (approval-gated): offers_create (title suffices — UI defaults +
  commercial default tax rate + numbering from settings), offers_update
  ({id, patch}), offers_set_status (draft→ready→accepted),
  offers_replace_blocks (block ids optional for new blocks),
  offers_delete (critical)

Skills corrected to match reality: status enum is ready (not done),
offers_update takes {id, patch}, status changes via offers_set_status.
The in-editor draft patch tool additionally allows the phase/tax display
toggles so on-page parity matches offers_update.

commits.message:
offers: retire frontend edit tools — agents write via backend ops, editor follows live

The offers_apply_draft_patch / offers_apply_blocks_patch frontend tools
were the wrong write path: they only existed while the edit page was
open in the chatting tab, staged changes invisibly to the agent's own
reads (endless "try again" loops), required a raw suspend/confirm/resume
per edit, and bypassed the durable-grant approval system.

Agents now edit exclusively through offers_update / offers_replace_blocks
(approval-gated, works from any page/task/background). The editor already
had a realtime binding on offers + offer_blocks "regardless of writer" —
it just never adopted refetches after the initial seed:

- adopt external writes live when local state is pristine
  (reference-equality against the last adopted server snapshot)
- amber conflict banner when unsaved local edits exist:
  "Änderungen laden" / "Meine Version behalten"
- save marks local state adopted so the save-triggered refetch doesn't
  flag a false conflict

Skills rewritten to the backend-only flow (no in-page tool sections;
note that open editors reflect writes live).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.message:
realtime: fix ai.thread_participant RLS recursion + de-latch live-cache gates

The thread_participant select policy checked membership by querying
thread_participant itself — infinite recursion whenever evaluated as a
non-bypassing role. Only Realtime's WALRUS does that (the API uses the
service role), and one poisoned row aborted realtime.list_changes for the
whole WAL batch, killing live updates for every table. Membership check
moved to a security definer helper.

live-cache: claims sync now re-evaluates on auth state changes instead of
latching a one-shot result, and every not-subscribing path logs its reason.

commits.message:
contacts: fix backfill never reaching older unindexed contacts

backfill() scanned only the newest `limit` contacts and filtered for
missing/stale embeddings within that window, so once the newest `limit`
were indexed, repeated calls could never advance to older contacts.

Scan wide, work narrow (mirrors the inbox provider): load up to
MAX_STATUS_SCAN rows, filter missing/stale over the full window, then
slice target ids to `limit`. Extract the shared loadIndexState() helper
for getStatus() + backfill(), and cover the window behavior with a test.

commits.message:
pdf-templates: stop seed-snapshots shadowing provider default templates

Tenant default templates were stored as verbatim snapshots of the provider
defaults on first save, so provider template improvements never reached
tenants again. Markup columns are now nullable: NULL means "follow the
module provider's built-in default", resolved at render time. Writes
normalize markup equal to the current provider default back to NULL
(normalizePdfTemplateMarkup, applied in the DAL on create/update), and the
offers/invoices render paths fall back per-field to the provider defaults.

Migration drops NOT NULL and one-time-repairs never-re-saved rows
(created_at = updated_at) to NULL; rows saved again later may carry real
customizations and are left untouched.

Note: pdfTemplateInputSchema deliberately avoids .default(null) on the
markup fields — zod 4 applies defaults for absent keys even through
.partial(), so a name-only PATCH would have reset custom markup
(regression-tested in types.test.ts).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

realtime: isolate live-cache channels per binding + fix team binding

Root cause of dead module realtime (verified in-browser): the team live
binding listed team-hr tables (employees, contracts, gallery photos) that
this installation never created — realtime creates all of a channel's
postgres_changes subscriptions in ONE transaction, so the missing table
rolled back every module's subscription on the shared live-data channel.

  team-hr registers its own binding when it lands
- useLiveCache subscribes one channel per module binding so a broken
  binding only degrades its own module (verified: 22 subscriptions
  registered, SQL write appeared live in the open offer editor)

  chat and asking permission — the approval prompt is the gate

commits.message:
copilot: source compact-surface HITL interrupt from the gated dockInterrupt

The bottom dock / floating launcher approval card never appeared because the
surfaces layer read `injected.openInterrupt` — a field the copilot session
never populates (it exposes `openInterruptFromSession`), and it also skipped
the `pendingInterruptToolCallIds` gate. So `compactInterruptContent` was
always null.

Fix: build the interrupt banner once in the drawer body from the authoritative,
gated `dockInterrupt` (same node the docked panel's `dockedInterruptSurface`
uses, with `session.respond` for decisions/approvals) and pass it into the
surface tree. Bottom dock and floating launcher now show the exact approval
card the docked panel does.

commits.message:
ai: stop Mastra thread saves from resurrecting cleared HITL interrupts

The approval card reappeared on every reload after a successful approve:
resume cleared ag_ui_open_interrupt via updateSessionForUser, then the
parked Mastra session's final thread save wrote its LOAD-TIME metadata
snapshot back ~2s later — resurrecting the interrupt (and the DB poll
showed exactly cleared→restored). The old guard only carried the DB value
forward when the snapshot LACKED the key, assuming in-memory metadata
never contains it — false on a parked tool-approval resume, where the
thread was loaded while the interrupt was set.

Treat the HITL keys (open interrupt + tool-approval grants) as DB-owned:
on every adapter save, resolve them from the current row — never add or
remove them based on the in-memory snapshot.

Verified end-to-end: approve → op executes → metadata poll shows the
interrupt cleared and STAYING cleared → reload shows no card.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.message:
offers: normalize agent blocks to the schema the editor actually renders

'Add 3 phases with dummy positions' produced structurally perfect agent
writes that rendered as an empty, phaseless, 0-priced offer. Two schema
truths nobody had written down:

1. The rendering stack (ItemBlockRow, HeadlineBlock/TextBlock, PDF
   provider, phase grouping) reads amount/cost_per_item/tax and
   title/content — NOT the quantity/unit_price/tax_rate/text shape that
   the stale createEmptyBlock helper suggests and that models guess.
2. There is no rendered "phase" block type at all: a phase is a headline
   block with is_phase: true (isPhaseHeadlineBlock), name in title.

offers_replace_blocks now normalizes agent input at the write boundary —
alias keys are converted and dropped (so a later manual edit cannot
diverge from a stale alias copy) and type:"phase" becomes
headline+is_phase. The tool description and the offers-blocks-management
skill now document the true canonical schema with a worked example (the
skill previously taught the broken field names).

Also fixes the agent-session-realtime test mock to capture only the
postgres_changes callback (a system-error listener registers after it
since d8522c4).

commits.message:
refactor(connections): nest connector providers under modules/connections/providers/*

Move connections-google, connections-microsoft, and connections-slack from
top-level modules/ into modules/connections/providers/{google,microsoft,slack}
as nested workspace plugin packages. Package names and engenty.plugins slugs are
unchanged (@engenty/connections-google, …) — the slug is now taken from each
nested manifest's `id`, discovered by a `providers/*` convention (only that
literal segment is scanned one level deeper).

Both plugin-resolution SSOTs (scripts/lib/engenty-modules.mjs and
@engenty/environment) gain listWorkspaceModulesOnDisk with fail-loud guards
(nested id required, slug collisions and package-name/id mismatches throw), and
resolveEnabledModules resolves nested dirs. Runtime discovery, the manifest
conventional-root check, and every one-level module scanner (migration
aggregation, storage-bucket sync, ui-dep sync, module-boundary + supabase-import
checks, ai-check, env contributions, the UI plugin-artifact generator, and vite
UI aliases) are nested-aware. The loader now emits an error diagnostic for any
enabled module with no discovered candidate, so a future path regression fails
loud instead of silently dropping a plugin.

Generated artifacts (.env.example, generated-catalog.ts, supabase config) are
byte-identical; only pnpm-lock importer paths move.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(connections): add browser + api_key auth kinds

Generalize ConnectorDefinition.auth from oauth2-only to a discriminated union
(oauth2 | api_key | browser):

commits.message:
feat(connections-sdk): ConnectorFilesCapability + synthesized files_* actions

A connector may declare a `files` capability (list/read/stat + optional search
over provider-native refs). defineConnector synthesizes read actions from it
(files_list/files_read/files_stat/files_search), so they project as gateway
operations and inherit policy, approvals, audit, and agent tools with no extra
code. The read result is discriminated (url | base64 | text) so each provider
returns its cheapest shape. The module client gains listFileSources / filesList
/ filesRead / filesStat, routed through callAction (read-gated like any action).

commits.message:
feat(connections): local-files connector via a browser File System Access bridge

A read-only connector for local folders the user grants in their browser. Each
granted directory is one browser-auth connection ("account"); the connector
declares the files capability, so its list/read/stat/search actions round-trip
into the tab that holds the directory handle:

- src: module_local_files schema (installations, directories, bridge_requests),
  the bridge server (liveness fail-fast → enqueue → poll), the connector, and
  authenticated routes (register directory, heartbeat, claim, respond,
  reactivate). connections-sdk gains repo.setConnectionStatus.
- ui: an always-mounted bridge (new `backgroundComponents` UI-plugin seam)
  that heartbeats and drains requests via the File System Access API against
  IndexedDB-persisted handles; a "Connect folder" button (showDirectoryPicker),
  gated to Chromium. A globalThis-backed registry lets non-OAuth connectors
  supply their own connect affordance in the connections catalog.
- fix: the UI plugin-artifact generator's conventional-root check now accepts
  nested providers, so ui-bearing modules/*/providers/* enter the catalog.

Add the central retrieval service core (Phase 1)

SearchIndexProviders, so synthesized tools, event bindings, and the
/api/search-index/* surface work unchanged. Splitters (none/fixed/paragraph/
custom + Mastra via subpath export), per-tenant embedding models, batched
scan-wide/work-narrow backfill, fastPath/evaluator/hydrate/postRank retriever

FTS+trigram+vector fusion RPC; chunks PK is (tenant_id, id) — chunk ids are
doc-scoped, a global PK let one tenant's backfill overwrite another's (caught
by the E2E suite). Loader exposes registerRetrievalSource and registers
core_workspace_search on first use.

Design doc: docs/wip/retrieval-service.md. 24 unit + 8 E2E tests.

commits.message:
fix(plugins): discovery guard compares by dir, not package name

The fail-loud 'enabled module not discovered' guard compared enabled slugs
against candidate package names (idHint), so modules whose package name differs
from their slug (e.g. @engenty/files-ui for slug 'files', pdf-templates) warned
spuriously on every boot. Compare each enabled slug's resolved on-disk dir
(nested-aware via resolveModuleDir) against discovered candidate rootDirs
instead — still catches real path-resolution drops, no false positives.

commits.message: discovery guard compares by dir, not package name
commits.body:
The fail-loud 'enabled module not discovered' guard compared enabled slugs
against candidate package names (idHint), so modules whose package name differs
from their slug (e.g. @engenty/files-ui for slug 'files', pdf-templates) warned
spuriously on every boot. Compare each enabled slug's resolved on-disk dir
(nested-aware via resolveModuleDir) against discovered candidate rootDirs
instead — still catches real path-resolution drops, no false positives.

commits.body:
A connector may declare a `files` capability (list/read/stat + optional search
over provider-native refs). defineConnector synthesizes read actions from it

operations and inherit policy, approvals, audit, and agent tools with no extra
code. The read result is discriminated (url | base64 | text) so each provider
returns its cheapest shape. The module client gains listFileSources / filesList
/ filesRead / filesStat, routed through callAction (read-gated like any action).

commits.message: nest connector providers under modules/connections/providers/*
commits.body:
Move connections-google, connections-microsoft, and connections-slack from
top-level modules/ into modules/connections/providers/{google,microsoft,slack}
as nested workspace plugin packages. Package names and engenty.plugins slugs are
unchanged (@engenty/connections-google, …) — the slug is now taken from each
nested manifest's `id`, discovered by a `providers/*` convention (only that
literal segment is scanned one level deeper).

Both plugin-resolution SSOTs (scripts/lib/engenty-modules.mjs and
@engenty/environment) gain listWorkspaceModulesOnDisk with fail-loud guards
(nested id required, slug collisions and package-name/id mismatches throw), and
resolveEnabledModules resolves nested dirs. Runtime discovery, the manifest
conventional-root check, and every one-level module scanner (migration
aggregation, storage-bucket sync, ui-dep sync, module-boundary + supabase-import
checks, ai-check, env contributions, the UI plugin-artifact generator, and vite
UI aliases) are nested-aware. The loader now emits an error diagnostic for any
enabled module with no discovered candidate, so a future path regression fails
loud instead of silently dropping a plugin.

Generated artifacts (.env.example, generated-catalog.ts, supabase config) are
byte-identical; only pnpm-lock importer paths move.

commits.message: normalize agent blocks to the schema the editor actually renders
commits.body:
'Add 3 phases with dummy positions' produced structurally perfect agent
writes that rendered as an empty, phaseless, 0-priced offer. Two schema
truths nobody had written down:

1. The rendering stack (ItemBlockRow, HeadlineBlock/TextBlock, PDF
   provider, phase grouping) reads amount/cost_per_item/tax and
   title/content — NOT the quantity/unit_price/tax_rate/text shape that
   the stale createEmptyBlock helper suggests and that models guess.
2. There is no rendered "phase" block type at all: a phase is a headline
   block with is_phase: true (isPhaseHeadlineBlock), name in title.

offers_replace_blocks now normalizes agent input at the write boundary —
alias keys are converted and dropped (so a later manual edit cannot
diverge from a stale alias copy) and type:"phase" becomes
headline+is_phase. The tool description and the offers-blocks-management
skill now document the true canonical schema with a worked example (the
skill previously taught the broken field names).

Also fixes the agent-session-realtime test mock to capture only the
postgres_changes callback (a system-error listener registers after it
since d8522c4).

commits.message: stop Mastra thread saves from resurrecting cleared HITL interrupts
commits.body:
The approval card reappeared on every reload after a successful approve:
resume cleared ag_ui_open_interrupt via updateSessionForUser, then the
parked Mastra session's final thread save wrote its LOAD-TIME metadata
snapshot back ~2s later — resurrecting the interrupt (and the DB poll
showed exactly cleared→restored). The old guard only carried the DB value
forward when the snapshot LACKED the key, assuming in-memory metadata
never contains it — false on a parked tool-approval resume, where the
thread was loaded while the interrupt was set.

Treat the HITL keys (open interrupt + tool-approval grants) as DB-owned:
on every adapter save, resolve them from the current row — never add or
remove them based on the in-memory snapshot.

Verified end-to-end: approve → op executes → metadata poll shows the
interrupt cleared and STAYING cleared → reload shows no card.

commits.body:
Three compact-composer improvements to the floating launcher and bottom dock:

1. Honor an explicit "bottom" dock preference on tablet and mobile instead
   of collapsing to the side drawer — the bottom dock is a centered,
   max-width card that clamps to the viewport, so it works at any width.
   (sidebar still collapses to drawer on tablet since it needs inline room.)

2. When the active thread already has a real back-and-forth, the status
   flap shows a one-line preview of the last assistant reply (expandable)
   instead of staying blank — so reopening the launcher/dock on an existing
   conversation shows continuity. Live status/errors still take precedence.

3. Add "Neuer Chat" to the composer (+) menu (routes through the same
   agent-aware new-chat handler as the panel header), so a fresh thread is
   one tap away from the compact surfaces.

binding listed team-hr tables (employees, contracts, gallery photos) that

rolled back every module's subscription on the shared live-data channel.

  binding only degrades its own module (verified: 22 subscriptions
  registered, SQL write appeared live in the open offer editor)
- offers skills: act directly on drafts instead of pasting content into
  chat and asking permission — the approval prompt is the gate

commits.message: stop seed-snapshots shadowing provider default templates
commits.body:
Tenant default templates were stored as verbatim snapshots of the provider
defaults on first save, so provider template improvements never reached
tenants again. Markup columns are now nullable: NULL means "follow the
module provider's built-in default", resolved at render time. Writes
normalize markup equal to the current provider default back to NULL
(normalizePdfTemplateMarkup, applied in the DAL on create/update), and the
offers/invoices render paths fall back per-field to the provider defaults.

Migration drops NOT NULL and one-time-repairs never-re-saved rows
(created_at = updated_at) to NULL; rows saved again later may carry real
customizations and are left untouched.

footers.value:
pdfTemplateInputSchema deliberately avoids .default(null) on the
markup fields — zod 4 applies defaults for absent keys even through
.partial(), so a name-only PATCH would have reset custom markup
(regression-tested in types.test.ts).

defaults on first save, so provider template improvements never reached
tenants again. Markup columns are now nullable: NULL means "follow the
module provider's built-in default", resolved at render time. Writes
normalize markup equal to the current provider default back to NULL
(normalizePdfTemplateMarkup, applied in the DAL on create/update), and the
offers/invoices render paths fall back per-field to the provider defaults.

Migration drops NOT NULL and one-time-repairs never-re-saved rows
(created_at = updated_at) to NULL; rows saved again later may carry real
customizations and are left untouched.

commits.message: fix backfill never reaching older unindexed contacts
commits.body:
backfill() scanned only the newest `limit` contacts and filtered for
missing/stale embeddings within that window, so once the newest `limit`
were indexed, repeated calls could never advance to older contacts.

Scan wide, work narrow (mirrors the inbox provider): load up to
MAX_STATUS_SCAN rows, filter missing/stale over the full window, then
slice target ids to `limit`. Extract the shared loadIndexState() helper
for getStatus() + backfill(), and cover the window behavior with a test.

commits.message: fix ai.thread_participant RLS recursion + de-latch live-cache gates
commits.body:
The thread_participant select policy checked membership by querying
thread_participant itself — infinite recursion whenever evaluated as a
non-bypassing role. Only Realtime's WALRUS does that (the API uses the
service role), and one poisoned row aborted realtime.list_changes for the
whole WAL batch, killing live updates for every table. Membership check
moved to a security definer helper.

footers.value:
claims sync now re-evaluates on auth state changes instead of
latching a one-shot result, and every not-subscribing path logs its reason.

commits.message: retire frontend edit tools — agents write via backend ops, editor follows live
commits.body:
The offers_apply_draft_patch / offers_apply_blocks_patch frontend tools
were the wrong write path: they only existed while the edit page was
open in the chatting tab, staged changes invisibly to the agent's own
reads (endless "try again" loops), required a raw suspend/confirm/resume
per edit, and bypassed the durable-grant approval system.

Agents now edit exclusively through offers_update / offers_replace_blocks
(approval-gated, works from any page/task/background). The editor already
had a realtime binding on offers + offer_blocks "regardless of writer" —
it just never adopted refetches after the initial seed:

- adopt external writes live when local state is pristine
  (reference-equality against the last adopted server snapshot)
- amber conflict banner when unsaved local edits exist:
  "Änderungen laden" / "Meine Version behalten"
- save marks local state adopted so the save-triggered refetch doesn't
  flag a false conflict

Skills rewritten to the backend-only flow (no in-page tool sections;
note that open editors reflect writes live).

commits.message: register the agent-facing module operations the skills describe
commits.body:
The offers.manager skills were written against offers_list/get/create/
update/get_blocks/replace_blocks/… — but the module only registered HTTP
routes, which never enter the tools catalog, so agents had ZERO backend
access to offers (invoices had the full layer; offers lost it in the
migration). Register the gateway methods (invoices pattern):

- reads: offers_list, offers_get (id or offer number), offers_get_blocks,
  offers_get_next_number
- writes (approval-gated): offers_create (title suffices — UI defaults +
  commercial default tax rate + numbering from settings), offers_update
  ({id, patch}), offers_set_status (draft→ready→accepted),
  offers_replace_blocks (block ids optional for new blocks),
  offers_delete (critical)

Skills corrected to match reality: status enum is ready (not done),
offers_update takes {id, patch}, status changes via offers_set_status.
The in-editor draft patch tool additionally allows the phase/tax display
toggles so on-page parity matches offers_update.

commits.message: dock floating launcher & avatar to bottom-right on mode switch
commits.body:
The floating compact launcher was positioned from floatingPosition, whose
default was sized to the modal (FLOATING_DEFAULT_HEIGHT=148) while the launcher
renders at ~56px — so switching to floating dropped it mid-screen, and nothing
re-cornered either surface on mode changes.

- Size the launcher's bottom-right home to its own footprint via
  resolveLauncherCornerPosition (used for the initial position too).
- Re-dock both surfaces to the corner when switching to floating/mini-floating
  from the position menu (launcher via floatingPosition, avatar via clearing
  fabPosition/anchor).
- Add a floatingDockedToCorner flag + layout effect that keeps the resting
  launcher pinned as its measured height settles; cleared once the user drags.
- reanchorFloatingPositionToViewport keeps a corner-docked panel tracking its
  edges on window resize instead of only clamping.

Verified in-app: switch->floating, switch->avatar, and reload all land
bottom-right; window resize tracks the corner.

commits.message: make drawer robust before layout hydration and sidebar mount
commits.body:
Harden copilot surface mounting against two races:

- Gate CopilotDrawerLayer until the persisted `copilot.layout` snapshot is
  applied (`copilotLayoutApplied`) so the drawer/FAB don't render with a
  stale default position before hydration.
- Track inline-sidebar mount state (`copilotSidebarReady` +
  notifySidebarMounted/Unmounted) to re-render when the portal target
  attaches, and fall back to the drawer SidePanel when the sidebar
  container isn't available while open (extracted `renderDrawerFallback`).
- Reconcile the persisted layout snapshot via reconcileCopilotLayoutSnapshot
  before applying it.

commits.message: keep floating avatar FAB on-screen
commits.body:
The Copilot floating avatar (CopilotFabTrigger) applied its persisted
`fabPosition` verbatim. A position saved on a larger window rendered the
FAB off the viewport edge on a smaller one, so the avatar silently
disappeared with no recovery. The existing viewport-clamp only covered
the open floating drawer, never the collapsed FAB.

Clamp the persisted position to the current viewport when resolving the
FAB anchor (re-applied on resize) and in resolveTriggerAnchor so drag
origin and speed-dial centering match the rendered position. Also reset
collapseToCircle when the drawer is open so the two states can't conflict.

`fabPosition` verbatim. A position saved on a larger window rendered the
FAB off the viewport edge on a smaller one, so the avatar silently
disappeared with no recovery. The existing viewport-clamp only covered
the open floating drawer, never the collapsed FAB.

Clamp the persisted position to the current viewport when resolving the
FAB anchor (re-applied on resize) and in resolveTriggerAnchor so drag
origin and speed-dial centering match the rendered position. Also reset
collapseToCircle when the drawer is open so the two states can't conflict.

commits.message: plugins install — surface db migrate next-step + opt-in --db-migrate (#6)
commits.body:
`plugins install` aggregates module migrations but never applies them, which
surprised users (install OK, UI then throws "Invalid schema"). After installing
in-repo workspace modules it now prints the next step ("run pnpm db:migrate"),
and a new opt-in `--db-migrate` flag applies them locally — gated on a reachable
local DB so install stays DB-free for CI, fresh checkouts, and remote databases.

commits.message: CI setup, UI build, catalog/AI test resilience + lint pass (#4)
commits.body:
* chore: full lint/format pass + fix UI build and module guardrail for company-profile

Run `pnpm fix` (ultracite) across the workspace and resolve everything needed
to make build, typecheck, lint and test green.

Substantive fixes (the rest is auto-formatting):
- ui/vite.config.ts: run module-UI alias discovery in build, not just dev. The
  generated plugin catalog imports `@engenty/<module>/ui/plugin` from source
  even though modules are never dependencies of the core shell; production build
  previously dropped those aliases, so the catalog's company-profile import
  failed to resolve. Now resolves module UI entrypoints to source in build too.
- plugins/loader.ts: split `??=` out of the `.push(...)` expression (no
  assignment-in-expression).
- environment/engenty-modules.ts + scripts/lib/engenty-modules.mjs: assign
  `undefined` instead of `delete` (JSON.stringify omits it; no delete operator).
- module-metadata-guardrails.test.ts: add company-profile to the frozen
  first-party guarded module set (added as a module in PR #2 but the list was
  never updated; it passes all metadata guardrails).

footers.value: pnpm lint, typecheck (51/51), build (38/38), test (2400 passed) green.

Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* chore(env): regenerate .env.example to match manifest

example:check failed in CI — the manifest's example default for
AI_GATEWAY_DEFAULT_MODEL had drifted from .env.example. Regenerated via
`pnpm env:example:write`.

Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(catalog-search): skip embedding when no gateway credentials

The catalog search embedding path issued a live AI Gateway call even with no
credentials, then caught the auth failure and fell back to lexical. On CI
(no API key / OIDC token) and slow shared runners that doomed round-trip could
exceed the 10s test timeout, flaking apps/ai and api tests that boot the app.

Short-circuit to lexical ranking when neither AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY nor
VERCEL_OIDC_TOKEN is set — behavior-equivalent (it fell back anyway) but fast
and deterministic, and quicker in any keyless environment. api-catalog tests
stub a key since they exercise the (mocked) embedding path.

Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(ci): run project setup script, not pnpm's builtin 'setup'

`pnpm setup` invokes pnpm's reserved built-in (configures PNPM_HOME), so the
project's "setup" script ('pnpm engenty setup') never ran in CI. That meant
supabase/migrations was never aggregated, so migration-reading tests
(supabase-sync-lib, live-cache) failed with ENOENT and createApp-based AI tests
hung. Use 'pnpm run setup' to invoke the package script.

This is why main's CI was red since the workflow landed.

Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(ai): skip background boot tasks under VITEST

createApp() starts a stalled-run sweep, the gateway model-sync scheduler, and
the task-dispatch consumer at boot — all of which do real DB/gateway I/O. In CI
(SUPABASE_URL points at a Supabase that isn't running) those calls retry with
backoff and blow the 10s test timeout, hanging app.test.ts and
search-index-registration.test.ts.

Gate all three on `process.env.VITEST`, consistent with the existing
'skip when a store is injected via options' convention. Verified by running
both suites against a dead SUPABASE_URL with no gateway key — 14/14 pass fast.

commits.message: prefer legacy JWT keys for local Supabase (#2)
commits.body:
* fix(env-setup): prefer legacy JWT keys when harvesting local Supabase status

The wizard resolved Supabase keys new-format-first (SECRET_KEY/
PUBLISHABLE_KEY), writing sb_secret_/sb_publishable_ values to .env.local.
The local Supabase CLI stack's PostgREST only validates HS256 JWTs against
JWT_SECRET and rejects the single-part sb_* keys (PGRST301) unless
asymmetric signing keys are configured — so dev:env:init produced a stack
that 500s on every request to a custom schema.

resolveSupabaseValue now takes a preferJwt option; the wizard sets it when
harvesting from 'supabase status' (always the local stack) so the legacy
3-part JWT keys win. Production/example preference for the new keys is
unchanged.

* docs(dev): add setup-process guide and expand plugin lifecycle docs

One verb per step: install/uninstall (in-repo slug or external package),
list (disk view, enriched when the API is up), interactive multi-select picker
with all/none/invert. create is now scaffold-only. Removes the redundant
wire-ui command and the manifest subcommand group; command groups print help
and exit 0 instead of cascading ERR_PNPM_RECURSIVE_EXEC.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.message: decouple context-graph into a self-registering plugin
commits.body:
Core no longer statically imports @engenty/context-graph. The plugin owns its
singletons and installs a host via engenty.server.registerContextGraphHost();
core holds only the plugin-sdk contract and delegates lazily. This makes the
core host plugins-free and removes the boot-time dist build it required.
